source.title: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs
source.authors: Amr Moustafa; Max Feser; Florian Mai

record.file_problem: The paper’s main text through the limitations is present, but the reference list is cut off after reference [9].
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates SAE-derived sparse features in Gemma-2-27B, an LLM setting, and reports their deception-detection results relative to dense activations. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition as background and uses sparse autoencoders to compare representations. The reported table measures deception-probe AUROC and recall, not feature recovery quality, completeness, stability, or geometric overlap. Rows below record the matched SAE-versus-dense probe results as indirect evidence for V4. The follow-up and upper-bound probes are included as reported in the table, though they are not direct tests of feature geometry.
record.test_reason: The study uses Gemma Scope SAE features (Gemma-2-27B, layer 31) only as an input space for deception probes. It reports probe AUROC and recall against dense activations. It does not measure whether features are distributed across neurons, whether the SAE recovers sparse or interpretable features, or any geometry, completeness or stability. Probe parity between SAE and dense inputs says nothing about whether superposition holds. This is the T4 case: the finding is relied on as a tool and only the study's own method's performance is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE features at ~66% depth do not consistently improve deception detectability over dense hidden states. SAE preserves the core signal, with benefits limited to some harm-pressure cases. They describe SAE features as an alternative rather than a reliably stronger representation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-derived sparse representations and deception probes in Gemma-2-27B; does not use the toy-network superposition setup or measure feature-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across evaluation datasets and probe families. The SAE comparison is restricted to Layer 31 (approximately 67.4% depth) and one model.

fits_no_version.finding: Deception probes on Gemma Scope SAE features (layer 31, Gemma-2-27B) reach roughly the same AUROC as probes on dense activations (average AUROC 0.53 dense vs similar or slightly lower SAE). Dense is slightly stronger overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature spaces preserve, but do not improve, linear separability of downstream concepts (deception) relative to dense activations.

record.problems: The SAE comparison uses one model and one layer. The authors report no exhaustive statistical significance testing; no uncertainty estimates are provided. Results do not directly assess SAE feature recovery or geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's aggregate average rows are omitted because the per-probe values are retained. No condition-specific AUROC or recall rows from Table 2 were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
No measure of feature spreading across neurons or of SAE feature recovery; SAE used only as probe input.
No completeness, stability or canonicity tests of SAE features.
No test of feature dimensionality. The INLP remarks concern the deception signal, not superposed features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification and its V4 labels are not justified. Equal probe performance on SAE and dense inputs bears on deception detection, not on whether LLMs superpose features or whether SAEs recover them. The file_problem is also inaccurate: references 10–24 appear in the text, only out of order. Results come from a single model and layer, with no significance testing.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension sweeps, overlap geometry, or sparsity-dependent transitions are tested.
No neuron polysemanticity or competition for representational capacity is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
Indirectly evaluates downstream deception detection using SAE features; does not measure how many neurons encode each feature or whether SAE features recover the model’s complete feature set.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CG evaluation set, direct probes using SAE features
reader_labels.reason: The SAE-feature probes show detectable signal on CG, with AUROC values above 0.50; see A01–A05.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GS, HP-C, and HP-KR evaluation sets; tested SAE-feature probes
reader_labels.reason: Results are near or below 0.50 in many settings and do not show a consistent advantage over dense activations; see A08–A12, A15–A19, and A22–A26.
